text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- New commercial television licence to be awarded to Ruutunelonen, controlled by Helsinki Media -- Social Democrat ministers provided the key support.
- Opinion poll shows a majority of Finns approve of Parliamentary Speaker Riitta Uosukainen's frank sexual revelations in her recent book.
- Investigations of police crime to be transferred to the public prosecutor.
- Finnyards may lose a billion markka order from Swedish Stena Line due to Stena's poor performance.
- Two thousand workers at Kvaerner Masa-Yards staged a walk-out to protest at the shipyard's plans to sub-contract more work.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Central government bureaucracy holding up many EU-funded projects in Finland's regions.
- Downswing in the sawmill industry finally bottoming out, with prices now edging upward.
- Valmet Automotive chief says the unit is not for sale.
- Valmet will double sub-contracting in a few years, CEO Matti Sundberg says.
- Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said Finland has become the target of international "Eco-fascism" and called on environmental organisations to cooperate with industry.
DEMARI

- Prime Minister Lipponen told Parliament the opposition Centre Party was fanning the flames of social bitterness and despair, after opposition leader Esko Aho called the government's unemployment policy a total failure.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Forestry group Metsa-Serla's new fine-paper machine at Kirkniemi mill starts up with prices in a slump.
- Banks trying to collect old loan guarantees -- Financial Supervision says practice is "unreasonable."
- Opinion poll shows the small Young Finns' party is likely to win one of Finland's 16 European Parliament seats, with candidate Jaakko Iloniemi seen strong.
- National Board of Forestry land-use plan calls for State to sell about 3,000 lakeside building plots over the next 10 years. Plots could be exchanged for conservation land.
AAMULEHTI
- Sixteen Finnish newspapers joining forces in a unique cooperation project to publish a weekly television supplement, "Treffi".
